                    ### Question
                    A previously healthy 26-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after collapsing during soccer practice. The patient appears well. His pulse is 73/min and blood pressure is 125/78 mm Hg. Cardiac examination is shown. Rapid squatting decreases the intensity of the patient's auscultation finding. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Asymmetric hypertrophy of the septum
opb. Fibrinoid necrosis of the mitral valve
opc. Eccentric dilatation of the left ventricle
opd. Calcification of the aortic valve
ope. Dilation of the aortic root

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The most likely cause of this patient's condition is asymmetric hypertrophy of the septum, specifically hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy. The rapid squatting decreasing the intensity of the auscultation finding is a classic feature of this condition. The evidence paths support the association between auscultation findings and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, confirming the likelihood of this diagnosis.
